## Summary

I implemented OpenAI Batch API support for the document extraction library across two files.

### New file: `langextract/providers/openai_batch.py`

- **`BatchConfig`** dataclass with `enabled`, `threshold`, `completion_window` (default `'24h'`), `poll_interval`, `timeout` (default `90000` > 86400), `max_requests_per_job`, `metadata` (default `None`), `on_job_create` (default `None`). Validates `completion_window` on construction — any value other than `'24h'` raises `ValueError` mentioning `completion_window`.
- **`BatchConfig.from_dict`** returns a `BatchConfig` unchanged, maps `True`/`False` to `BatchConfig(enabled=...)`, treats `None` as disabled, coerces mappings, and raises `TypeError` (`'batch must be a mapping'`) for anything else (e.g. a list).
- **`infer_batch`** — assigns `idx-{n:06d}` custom IDs, splits prompts into sub-batches of at most `batch_size` (also capped by `max_requests_per_job`), submits each as a separate job, and merges results in original order. It handles every specified error condition: `batch_size <= 0` (`InferenceConfigError`), job-create failure (deletes the input file, raises `'job create failed'`), terminal statuses (`status={status}`, plus error-field text), missing output/error files, per-item errors, non-2xx `status_code={code}`, refusals, missing/unexpected custom IDs (warning), 403 download retries (3 attempts / 2 sleeps → `'Files Read permission'`), error-file extraction when both files exist, and timeout (cancels the job, raises `'timed out'`). It forwards `metadata`, `completion_window`, invokes `on_job_create`, and uses `time.sleep`/`time.time`.

### Modified: `langextract/providers/openai.py`

- Constructor accepts `batch` (dict/bool/BatchConfig) and `seed`; batch config is stored in `_batch_cfg` and **not** forwarded to the chat completions API.
- Added `_build_batch_request` (includes `response_format` and `seed`) and `infer_batch`, which calls `openai_batch.infer_batch` and returns a list of single-element `ScoredOutput` lists.
- `infer` routes to batch mode when enabled and prompt count ≥ threshold, logs an INFO `'below the threshold'` message and falls back to real-time otherwise, and lets `InferenceConfigError` propagate. I also injected `self.seed` into the real-time config path so the existing `seed` kwarg test still passes.
